speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your episodes of unresponsiveness and facial grimacing, can you describe what happens right before an episode starts, and do you have any awareness during the event itself?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history; the "muddy taste" serves as a distinct aura, which strongly suggests a focal onset. I would like to know if there is any history of head trauma, fever, or seizures in your family, and have you noticed any triggers like lack of sleep or flashing lights? REQUEST TEST: EEG
